open_items: ILO direct-path 403 flap: fifth occurrence at cycle 202 (2026-08-11T00:01:22Z) - 9 of 12 contract assertions broken (auth:listing, constraint:availableconstraint, errors:missing_artefact, references:all, children, contentconstraint, descendants, none, parentsandsiblings; references:parents stayed ok), close to the broadest occurrence yet (cycle 159, 10 of 12). Basic gateway/direct health checks stayed healthy. Unlike the prior four occurrences, still showed mixed 200/403 responses on a live recheck ~40 min after the cycle started - not confirmed clean yet. Prior occurrences: cycle 32, cycle 94, cycle 159 (10 of 12), cycle 166 (5 of 12), all resolved within one cycle. Next run must confirm this one has cleared; if it spans a second full cycle that is new territory for this pattern. IMPORTANT: /api/history's per-endpoint status/failing series does NOT reflect contract-probe-only degradation - every run must check intermediate cycles individually via /api/cycle/{id} or by re-fetching /api/status, not rely on /api/history or /api/contracts changes (which only diffs the two newest cycles) alone.

ECB metadata 503 (provider_down): occurred cycle 199 only, resolved by cycle 200, clean through cycle 202 (3 consecutive healthy cycles). Different failure mode than the resolved ECB 406 issue and the ECB references:* 504 flap below. Watch for a second occurrence; escalate if a second episode does not resolve within a cycle or two.

ABS gateway metadata 502 Bad Gateway flap: occurred cycle 198 only, resolved by cycle 199, clean through cycle 202. Distinct from the ABS empty-error-body flap below (this one carried a real error message). Watch for recurrence.

ABS gateway metadata empty-error-body flap: fifth occurrence was cycles 150-152 (longest yet, 3 consecutive cycles), clean through cycle 202 (no new occurrence, 51 consecutive healthy cycles for this specific empty-message shape). Empty error message itself still worth fixing under code-change scope (GatewayError/next_step in monitor/checks_gateway.py). Watch for a sixth occurrence.

UNICEF direct-path HTTP 404 'no data found' flap: occurred cycle 197 only, resolved by cycle 198, clean through cycle 202. Different shape than the UNICEF 429 flap below. Watch for a second occurrence.

ILO references:contentconstraint ignored-vs-ok blip: one-cycle noise at cycle 199 only (verdict read ok instead of ignored; live recheck confirmed the parameter is still silently dropped in substance). No recurrence through cycle 202. Watch for recurrence; if it persists, revisit as a possible real behavior change.

ESTAT list_dataflows timeout pattern: ninth episode (cycles 144-145) resolved by cycle 146, clean through cycle 202 (57 consecutive healthy cycles). No fix applied under docs-only scope; standing recommendation (raise deadline, stream listing, or cache parsed result) carried forward for a session with code-change scope.
STATSNZ auth:listing capability_appeared, first seen cycle 60, still present at cycle 202: listing served without credentials. Still open, not re-reported since no new change.

Content-Type parameter order (charset vs version) on structure responses varies between requests, seen on ABS, OECD, ILO, and FBOS. Cosmetic, verdict stays ok. Expected to keep flapping across multiple endpoints; do not re-report unless the verdict itself changes.

IMF references:* 401 flap: first and only occurrence, cycle 161, resolved by cycle 162, clean through cycle 202. Same shape as the recurring ILO 403 flap (probe volume tripping provider-side throttling). Watch for a second occurrence.

UNICEF direct-path HTTP 429 flap: second occurrence at cycle 178, resolved by that run's live recheck. First occurrence cycle 126, resolved cycle 127. No recurrence through cycle 202. Watch for a third occurrence.
